title: [platform] list_enterprise_source_stubs error keeps happening
body:
### Helm Chart Version

1.3.1

### What step the error happened?

On deploy

### Relevant information

Hey folks, I am trying to deploy airbyte in an on-prem environment using helm charts, I use this command to install the helm chart.
```
helm install airbyte airbyte/airbyte --set minio.image.repository=quay.io/minio/minio --set minio.image.tag=RELEASE.2024-01-01T16-36-33Z-cpuv1 --namespace airbyte
```
After the installation happens and everything in clean, i get the same error in my source and destinations, here is the error, i have extracted the error from the airbyte server pod

I have tried putting the value of ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL to empty using this env var in my helm values 
```
ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL: ""
```
but the issue still exists, any idea what's wrong!?

This has now been resolved. For OSS, one more restart of the server pods may be required to make sure the cache is busted.

This is a separate problem from what was going on in this issue, but thought I'd chime in here in case you or others ran into this instead.

comments.author: hvignolo87
comments.body:
I was facing the same issue, and found a simpler workaround.

We need a response body like `[]` to solve the problem. This is achievable by setting the env var `ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?userId=999999`.

So we can simply add something like this in the server values:
```yaml
extraEnv:
  - key: ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL
  - value: "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?userId=999999"
```

Also we can manually modify the env var in the `configMap`.

Did you deploy the changes and the server pod have been restarted after that?

Please double check if you've used `extraEnv` or `extraEnvs`.

If yes, just manually edit the `configMap` and let the server pod restart to fetch the new value.

comments.author: marcosmarxm
comments.body: Hello 👋 I raised this to the platform team to investigate a solution. The last time it was a cache problem.

comments.author: pedroslopez
comments.body:
Hi folks - we made a change to the `connector_stubs.json` that should not have been applied to the `v0` endpoint, which inadvertently reintroduced the issue. I've reverted the change to v0, so a restart of the airbyte-server (to ensure cache is busted) should return to a working state.

As a note, later versions of Airbyte were updated when this originally happened so that any issue loading this endpoint does not impact the webapp or normal use of Airbyte, so I'd recommend updating Airbyte if possible.

comments.author: mateocolina
comments.body:
In our case, the issue was that we don't allow public internet access from our Kubernetes cluster. We fixed it, by manually downloading the json file and just creating a small proxy server that serves this json file, then redirect the bootloader to this proxy by setting CONNECTOR_REGISTRY_BASE_URL.

Successfully upgraded then to the next Airbyte version.
